topics.topic: Whether the UUID record-identity rule applies to AuditEntry
questions: Is an AuditEntry’s Registry-minted identity its ordinal sequence number, or must every AuditEntry have a UUID identity under the changed record-identity rule?

quotes:
Every identity of a record Registry mints — `project_id`, `room_id`,
  artifact pointer id, `customer_ref` — is an opaque identifier with no meaning in its form. Its
  concrete format is a UUID, as the v1 ids are; the import keeps every v1
  project, room and pointer id verbatim (R0-44, R0-50, R0-79).

its sequence number, minted by Registry: 1 for the store's first entry, then
  one more than the last its store's history ever wrote; never reused within
  that history, also after old entries are erased (R0-66), so the log's order
  is the order of the numbers even where two entries share an instant (owner,
  2026-10-31; codex round-02 T2). A store restored from a backup after a loss
  begins its own history from the backup's last number (R0-89);

Substitution: two entries with equal facts are two events — two archivings of
two projects at the same instant, or an erasure and its re-run — and the log
is read in time order as distinct entries (R0-58); the sequence number is what
tells them apart.
judgement.divergence: One implementation gives each AuditEntry a UUID identity under the general record-identity rule; another uses the ordinal sequence number as its identity under M09, which the owner reading the audit log and implementations persisting or referencing entries notice.
judgement.why: The general UUID rule covers every Registry-minted record identity, while M09 makes the Registry-minted ordinal sequence number the value that distinguishes AuditEntry entities.

witness.initial: A fresh Registry store has no audit entries.
events: The owner creates the first project.
Registry records the audit entry for that accepted project creation.
outcomes: The AuditEntry receives a UUID identity under the general record-identity rule.
The AuditEntry is identified by sequence number 1 under M09.
witness.observer: The owner reading the audit log and any implementation persisting or referencing AuditEntry identities.
basis:
The acting principal of a creation or a correction is the owner, always
(Primary actions): the project keeps no "created by".

The actions that write an entry (R0-58): creating, correcting, archiving,
  anonymising and deleting a project; recording, correcting and erasing a
  customer; restricting and lifting; ending and resuming a relationship;
  granting a project to a session and revoking one; the import, as one entry
  naming the migration closure (M10) by its file digest; erasing old entries.

topics.topic: Whether the UUID record-identity rule applies to OwnerSession
questions: Is an OwnerSession a “record” for the first rule, or is its identity expressly excluded from the UUID rule?

quotes:
Two further identifiers Registry mints are opaque too: the owner session's
  (M11), at least 32 random bytes (State 2 A13 rule 7), and the confirmation
  id, a UUID.
judgement.why: The text expressly treats the OwnerSession identity as a further identifier with at least 32 random bytes while separately specifying that the confirmation id is a UUID.
